sources.entry: tinytag - A library for reading audio file metadata of MP3, MP4, WAV, OGG, FLAC, WMA, and AIFF files.

summary.one_liner: tinytag is a pure-Python library for reading metadata, embedded images and audio properties from MP3, MP4/M4A, WAV, OGG, FLAC, WMA/ASF and AIFF files.
summary.what_it_does: It parses ID3v1/v2 tags, MP4 atoms, RIFF/WAV chunks, Vorbis/Opus/Speex/FLAC comments, ASF objects and AIFF chunks through one common API. It exposes common fields such as artist, album, title, track, year, genre and duration, plus a flat "other" dictionary for extra or format-specific fields. Embedded images can be read with image=True and accessed by kind, such as front cover. It also reports audio properties like bitrate, samplerate, channels, bit depth, lossless flag and MIME/codec type. A command-line module (python3 -m tinytag) prints metadata as JSON, and it can read from file-like objects. It is read-only; writing tags is out of scope.
use_cases: read artist, album and title from music files
get duration or bitrate of audio files
list audio file metadata from the command line
identify codec or MIME type of an audio file
read tags from in-memory BytesIO audio data
notable: Same API across MP3, MP4, WAV, OGG, FLAC, WMA and AIFF formats
Pure Python with no third-party dependencies
Embedded image extraction by standardized kind, e.g. front_cover
Optional magic-byte detection, which can be disabled
Read-only by design; the README points to Mutagen or pytaglib for writing
caveats: Cannot write or change metadata; the README recommends Mutagen or pytaglib for that
The ignore_errors parameter and tag.audio_offset attribute are obsolete and slated for removal
The 'extra' dictionary and get_image() are deprecated in favour of 'other' and images.any
